submission.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies across all three candidate absorber materials and various plate thicknesses within the allowed range (2-10mm), Absorber-F2 at 4.0mm plate thickness delivers the best energy resolution of 3.084% at 100 GeV. This represents a significant improvement over the other candidates: Absorber-F1 achieves 3.814% at its optimal thickness (4.5mm), while Absorber-F3 achieves 4.973% at 5.0mm. The simulation explored thicknesses from 3mm to 6mm for all materials, with fine-grained searches around the optimal points. The 4.0mm thickness for Absorber-F2 sits at the minimum of the resolution curve. All project documents indicate that Absorber-F2 is mechanically compatible with the design, can be machined to required tolerances, and no documentation suggests incompatibility with the hands-on maintenance requirement. This recommendation optimizes the primary goal of achieving the best possible energy resolution while satisfying all constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 at 4.0mm achieves 3.084% resolution, better than F1 (3.814% at 4.5mm) and F3 (4.973% at 5.0mm)

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F2 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as one of three candidate absorber materials

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: No documentation found indicating incompatibility of Absorber-F2 with hands-on maintenance. Meeting notes state mechanical design is compatible with every candidate absorber.
Recommended thickness of 4.0mm falls within the required range of 2-10mm
